T430 (doctor lies clean) — closed. The defect, verified at HEAD before any edit: `bin/argus --mode doctor` printed a permanently-green one-line console verdict. bin/argus:1904 (as the brief located it) filtered findings by sweep grades (must/critical/should) while every doctor finding is graded 'could', so the filter matched nothing on every run and the console said 'argus: clean — no violations' while the report file carried NEEDS ACTION items. Plus the second defect: `--dry-run` dumped the ACCUMULATED JSONL log from a fixed /tmp/argus-dryrun-watchdog.md, so findings from previous runs printed as if current, and `--log <path>` did not redirect it (the fixed /tmp path also being a volatile-evidence citation in a tool that reports on volatile citations).

STATE AT START: the console-text half of the fix was ALREADY committed by T441 (2849ef8, 'make the observation layer say only what it can support') — at HEAD, the doctor console line derives from the doctor's own section counts. The brief's part 2 (derive the summary from the doctor's own sections) was therefore already landed; what remained was the brief's part 1 (deterministic seeded/null/freshness arms — the pre-existing arm 16 is state-dependent: it only asserts the non-clean console when the LIVE tree happens to have NEEDS ACTION, a state-dependent reading wearing a test's clothes), part 3 (the exit-code decision, never made), the second defect (dry-run freshness, still broken at HEAD), and the Orchestrator's added requirement (permanent non-fixture-live-add arm).

EXIT-CODE DECISION (brief part 3, on the record): `--mode doctor` NOW EXITS 1 when its NEEDS ACTION section is non-empty, 0 otherwise. Weighing: FOR — the seeded arm's requirement is explicit ('its exit status must distinguish it'), and a one-line check that automation can gate on needs a machine-readable verdict; text alone is exactly the permanently-green control this task exists to kill; the doctor already classifies the C10 citations under NEEDS ACTION in its report, so the code aligns the machine signal with the report's own classification. AGAINST — the brief's weighing that an exit-non-zero doctor 'turns 893 pre-existing C10 citations into a red suite'. That premise does not hold at the current wiring: `zig build test` runs tools/regression-argus-doctor.sh and the suite's exit code is its OWN FAIL flag; every doctor invocation inside the suite either ignores the doctor's RC (arms 0/1/6/8/9/14/16/18 via run_doctor/run_doctor_live/run_doctor_scrap) or asserts the new contract deterministically against scratch states (new arms 21/22). Verified by construction: with the fix in, a full suite run exits per the FAIL flag, not the doctor's RC, and the live-tree doctor run exits 1 only as a direct operator invocation. The one residual risk is a FUTURE consumer that propagates the doctor's RC against live-tree state — mitigated by making the suite's own arms exemplary (deterministic scratch-state assertions only) and by this record. The C10 standing-debt concern is unchanged: C10 stays report-only for claimlint's floor; the doctor's exit code reflects its own NEEDS ACTION classification, which already contains C10. Chose exit-1; the alternative ('console text honest, exit code unchanged') is documented as rejected because it cannot satisfy the arm requirement and leaves the check ungated for automation.

FRESHNESS FIX (second defect): dry-run now (1) prints ONLY the current run's entries — the dump filters the JSONL by run id; (2) honors explicit --log/--summary/--report instead of silently clobbering them; (3) defaults to a unique per-run temp file (tempfile.mkstemp, unlinked so a run that dies before writing leaves nothing) instead of the fixed shared /tmp paths, so consecutive dry-runs never share state. To make the run-id filter sound, run ids gained millisecond resolution (_utc_compact now emits YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSmmm): at second resolution two back-to-back runs shared an id and the filter could not separate them (the summary's last-run filter had the same latent issue). No consumer parses the run-id format (checked: it is only stored in log entries, displayed in the report header, and used as a filter key).
